mo_binder_pro.name: Binder Pro
mo_binder_pro.key: Per 2 capsules: 500 mg apple pectin, 300 mg humic-fulvic complex (Humiplex), 300 mg chlorella
mo_binder_pro.src: Label: Binder Pro sell sheet ND1141 Rev. 12/25 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/Binder Pro SS ND1141.pdf), opened by the mold agent 2026-11-03. Supplement Facts, serving 2 capsules, 30/60 servings: Apple Pectin 500 mg; Humic Fulvic Carbon Complex (25% humic acid, 6% fulvic acid) (Humiplex) 300 mg; Chlorella Algae (Chlorella vulgaris) 300 mg. Other ingredients: hypromellose, vegetable magnesium stearate, silica (no charcoal, no clay: Asher's email to a practice, 2026-10-29, 'Binder Pro has no charcoal or clay'). Label directions 'Take two capsules daily'; caution 'If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult'. Same amounts in scratchpad labels/labels.json (R178 / R178L) and in the products DB R178 (CellCore chart, catalog ND143 10/1/26). Sizes R178 60C and R178L 120C (ND144 price list 10/1/26, via labels.json). DOSE: NutriDyn's KBMO Mycotoxin Protocol ND1610 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/KBMO Practitioner Tools/KBMO Mycotoxin Protocol ND1610.pdf, opened 2026-11-03): 'Take 2 capsules twice daily.' TIMING: every NutriDyn educator mold grid puts the binder at Mid Morning and Mid Evening, apart from the breakfast and supper supplements (the educator's 'Mold Care ~ Preparation Plan' in the educator's 2025 seminar Rx PDF: 'BinderPro 1-2 / 1-2', layout text read 2026-11-03). The dose bar reads '2 capsules twice daily' (ND1610's own 'twice daily', so the bar names its frequency like the other four; polish round 1) over 'between meals, as directed' (polish round 2: ND1610's 4 a day is twice the label's 'Take two capsules daily', and 'as directed' matches the label's own 'or as directed by your healthcare practitioner', so a pharmacist checking the sheet against the bottle reads a directed dose, not a misprint), and the daily rhythm writes those between-meal slots as '2 hours after breakfast' and '2 hours after supper', so no box header can mislead: the morning dose is listed last in the Morning box, the evening dose sits in Bedtime (the rhythm's only box after supper) with its real time written on it. The 2-hour figure is NutriDyn product-support guidance for its charcoal binder GI Detox (email, 2026-10-29: 'it must be taken at least 2 hours away from food'), applied to Binder Pro; ND1141, ND1610 and the educator's grids give no hour figure. The check panel's rule (2 hours from food, other supplements and every medicine) matches. Photo: img-src/R178.png is a soft 4x stopgap of the 89x160 chart thumbnail. The print-quality candidate is Dropbox /NutriDyn/Product Images/Product Images (1)/R178_Web (dated 2026-05-13, no file extension); Dropbox downloads are blocked from this cloud session (proxy 403), so it is not staged yet. The replacement must show the reformulated label (subtitle 'Detoxification Support for Healthy Gut Barrier Function', ND1141 Rev. 12/25), not the 2024 social-media images. LINK: no verified nutridyn.com product page for Binder Pro is on file (the /binder-pro slug in gut-overgrowth.json has no source), so the link falls back to the nutridyn.com catalog search.

mo_gi_defend.name: GI Defend
mo_gi_defend.key: Per scoop: 2.5 g ImmunoLin serum‑derived bovine immunoglobulin protein isolate
mo_gi_defend.src: Label: GI Defend sell sheet ND850 Rev. 12/24 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/GI Defend SS ND850.pdf), opened by the mold agent 2026-11-03 and re-read in the review round. Supplement Facts: serving size about 1 scoop (2.5 g), about 30 servings; calories 10, protein 2 g; Bovine Immunoglobulin Protein Isolate (ImmunoLin) 2.5 g; other ingredients none. Directions 'Mix 1 scoop in 8 ounces of water or your favorite beverage'. Caution (re-read with the Dropbox fetch tool in polish round 1): 'If pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use. Keep out of reach of children.' The label prints no beef-allergy caution, but the powder is made from beef serum: the panel lists Bovine Immunoglobulin Protein Isolate and says 'Contains less than 0.05% fractionated bovine blood' (it is badged dairy-free because the isolate is serum-derived, not from milk). Products made from mammals can carry alpha-gal and trigger alpha-gal syndrome, the red-meat allergy spread by lone star tick bites, most cases in the South (CDC alpha-gal syndrome pages, 'Products that may contain alpha-gal', as cited on the IBD and Joint Pain sheets), so both check panels end with 'Beef or red-meat (alpha-gal) allergy? Skip GI Defend.', the IBD sheet's exact wording for the same powder (polish round 2). The column sub-line 'immune proteins from cows' (polish round 1, in place of 'bovine immunoglobulins') names that bovine source in plain words. Claims used: 'Supports healthy gut barrier function'; 'works by binding, neutralizing, and removing toxins from the gut' (bullet 'Helps bind toxins in the gut': ND850's binding verb in two lines, so the five 'In each serving' headings line up; polish round 2). Products DB R191 agrees (2.5 g ImmunoLin per scoop; size R191 75G). PROTOCOL: KBMO Mycotoxin Protocol ND1610 lists GI Defend ('binding, neutralizing, and removing gut toxins'; '2 scoops ... once daily'); the sheet prints the label's 1 scoop and leaves a higher dose to the practitioner. The sheet says it helps bind toxins (ND850's wording) but never calls it a binder, and the 2-hour spacing rule names only Binder Pro: ImmunoLin is an immunoglobulin protein, not a broad adsorbent; Asher's email to a practice, 2023-12-21, says it 'stays in the gut'. TIMING: before breakfast, from NutriDyn's '60 Day Gut Repair and Detox' protocol doc (read 2026-11-03: GI Defend, 'Mix 1 scoop in 8 ounces of water ...', When to take 'Before Breakfast'), which also keeps it 2 hours from both Binder Pro doses (2 hours after breakfast and supper); no time of day is printed on the label or in ND1610. Photo: img-src/R191.png is a soft 4x stopgap of the 146x160 chart thumbnail. The print-quality candidate is Dropbox /NutriDyn/Product Images/Product Images (1)/R191_Web (dated 2026-05-13, no file extension); Dropbox downloads are blocked from this cloud session (proxy 403), so it is not staged yet. URL: products.py SLUGS gi_defend (NutriDyn 60-day protocol doc).

mo_lipo_flow.name: Lipo-Flow
mo_lipo_flow.key: Per 2 tablets: 400 mg artichoke, 250 mg dandelion, 200 mg beet, 150 mg inositol, 100 mg each of gentian, tangerine, taurine, methionine
mo_lipo_flow.src: Label: Lipo-Flow sell sheet ND606 Rev. 4/26 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/Lipo-Flow SS ND606.pdf), opened by the mold agent 2026-11-03. Supplement Facts, serving 2 tablets, 90 servings: Artichoke Extract (aerial parts) 400 mg; Dandelion Extract (root) 250 mg; Beet Powder (root) 200 mg; Inositol 150 mg; Tangerine Extract (peel) 100 mg (printed as 'tangerine'); Gentian Extract (root; Gentiana scabra) 100 mg; Taurine 100 mg; L-Methionine 100 mg. Directions 'Take two tablets with a meal three times daily'. Claims used: 'Promote healthy bile processes', 'Promote healthy liver function'; the sheet says artichoke and beet are choleretic and cholagogue, dandelion, tangerine and gentian cholagogue. Same panel in scratchpad labels/labels.json R863; the products DB R863 (CellCore charts) gives six of the eight amounts. Size R863 180T (ND144 price list 10/1/26). CAUTION (check panel, both editions): German Commission E monographs (Blumenthal M, ed., 1998): artichoke leaf and dandelion are contraindicated with bile-duct obstruction and, with gallstones, used only after consulting a physician; gentian root is contraindicated with gastric and duodenal ulcers; the artichoke-leaf monograph also rules it out with a known allergy to artichoke or other composites (Asteraceae, the daisy family, which takes in ragweed and dandelion), printed as 'a ragweed allergy' (polish round 1); the EU HMPC artichoke-leaf monograph also lists hypersensitivity to Asteraceae plants. With gallstones the pharmacy edition says 'Ask your pharmacist or your doctor', since the monographs want a physician first. The Lipo-Flow label caution is generic, 'If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use' (labels.json R863), and backs the check panel's pregnancy line. PROTOCOL: NutriDyn educator, Mold Care ~ Preparation Plan 'Lipo-Flow 1-3 breakfast, 1-3 supper' and Common Base Plan '1-2 / 1-2'; her key maps 'Biliary Efflux Support' to Lipo-Flow (the educator's 2025 seminar Rx PDF and her 'COVID & Mycotoxins Guides' PDF, 2024). The sheet's 2 tablets with breakfast and supper (4 a day) sits inside the label's 6 a day and the educator's grid; since the label's own dose is two tablets three times daily, the dose bar reads 'with meals, as directed' (polish round 2) and the daily rhythm shows the breakfast and supper doses. Stands in for the competitor's bitter-herb (gentian, artichoke) and bile columns: NutriDyn's official match for bile formulas (Core Level Bile, GB-Plus, Lipo-Gen, LV-GB Complex in the switch charts). Mold-owned key, so the shared lipo_flow line other sheets print is unchanged. Photo: img-src/R863.png is a soft 4x stopgap of the 87x160 chart thumbnail. The print-quality candidate is Dropbox /NutriDyn/Product Images/Product Images (1)/R863_Web (dated 2026-05-13, no file extension); Dropbox downloads are blocked from this cloud session (proxy 403), so it is not staged yet. URL: products.py SLUGS lipo_flow.

mo_glutathione.name: Liposomal Glutathione
mo_glutathione.key: Per dropper (1 mL): 100 mg reduced L‑glutathione, in liposomes made with sunflower lecithin
mo_glutathione.src: Label: Liposomal Glutathione sell sheet ND971 Rev. 8/24 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/Liposomal Glutathione SS ND971.pdf), opened by the mold agent 2026-11-03 and re-read in the review round. Supplement Facts: serving 1 dropper (1 mL), 60 servings; L-Glutathione (reduced) 100 mg. Other ingredients: purified water, vegetable glycerin, natural strawberry watermelon flavor, non-GMO sunflower lecithin, stevia leaf extract, organic cane alcohol. Directions 'Shake well. Take one full dropper (1 mL) 2-4 times daily'. Caution 'If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use' (re-read with the Dropbox fetch tool in polish round 2). Claims used, both from ND971's 'Additional benefits' list: 'Supports antioxidant health', 'Supports healthy glutathione levels' (tagline 'Bioavailable Antioxidant and Detox Support'). Products DB R2188 agrees on five chart reads (100 mg per 1 mL). Size R2188 60 mL (ND144 price list 10/1/26). PROTOCOL: NutriDyn educator, Mycotoxin Exposure/History - Prep for Mold Plan 'Glutathione/NAC* 1 breakfast, 1 supper' (the educator's 2025 seminar Rx PDF); 'Glutathione' is also in her BioToxins/Mycotoxins checklist. Her asterisk reads '*Awareness of Gliotoxin risks and Glutathione'; that caution is left to the provider and is not printed on this patient sheet (decision recorded 2026-11-03; Asher can ask for a clause in the practitioner edition). NutriDyn KBMO MIP Protocol ND1577: 'Liposomal Glutathione one full dropper (1 mL) twice daily'. Chosen over NAC-600 because Mito Recharge on the same sheet already carries 100 mg NAC. Twice daily sits inside the label's 2 to 4 times. 'Shake well' is on the label and stays on the bottle; it is off the dose bar for room. mo_mito.name: Mito Recharge
mo_mito.key: Per 3 capsules: 200 mg acetyl‑L‑carnitine HCl, 75 mg alpha‑lipoic + 45 mg R‑lipoic acid, 100 mg each of CoQ10, NAC and EGCG, 250 mcg vitamin K1
mo_mito.src: Label: Mito Recharge sell sheet ND812 Rev. 2/25 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/Mito Recharge SS ND812.pdf), opened by the mold agent 2026-11-03. Supplement Facts, serving 3 capsules, 30 servings: vitamin C 150 mg, vitamin E 25 mg, vitamin K1 (as phytonadione) 250 mcg, thiamin 25 mg, riboflavin 12 mg, niacin 12 mg NE, vitamin B6 (P5P) 7.5 mg, magnesium 75 mg, selenium 25 mcg, taurine 300 mg, acetyl-L-carnitine HCl 200 mg, resveratrol 100 mg, coenzyme Q10 100 mg, N-acetyl-L-cysteine 100 mg, EGCG (green tea extract) 100 mg, quercetin 100 mg, alpha-lipoic acid 75 mg, R-alpha-lipoic acid 45 mg, sulforaphane glucosinolate 15 mg, hydroxytyrosol 10 mg, PQQ 7 mg, mixed tocopherols 0.5 mg. Directions 'Take three capsules daily'. Caution 'If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use' (re-read with the Dropbox fetch tool in polish round 2). Claims used: 'Promote healthy mitochondria', 'Support healthy detoxification capacity'. The printed line gives the two lipoic acids as the label lists them (alpha-lipoic acid 75 mg, R-alpha-lipoic acid 45 mg, written '75 mg alpha-lipoic + 45 mg R-lipoic acid' as on the fatty-liver and lyme sheets), so a pharmacist holding the bottle can match each number (polish round 1; the earlier '120 mg lipoic acid' was a sum the label never prints); the carnitine is named the way ND812 prints it, 'Acetyl-L-Carnitine HCl 200 mg' (re-read in polish round 2), since the 200 mg is the weight of the HCl salt; taurine 300 mg is left off for room, which keeps the block at six lines; vitamin K1 stays because the warfarin note on this sheet relies on it. Products DB R167 corroborates the CoQ10, carnitine, NAC, lipoic acid, EGCG and vitamin amounts (Ortho, CellCore charts); size R167 90C. PROTOCOL: NutriDyn educator, Mold Care ~ Preparation Plan 'Mito Recharge 1-3 breakfast, 1-3 supper' (the educator's 2025 seminar Rx PDF); the sheet prints the label's 3 a day, all with breakfast (food for the CoQ10 and the green tea extract). NutriDyn's official match for the competitor's mitochondrial column. Mold-owned key, so the lyme sheet's override of the shared 'mito' key never changes this page.
